text: Be not afraid, for I am with you always.
author: Isaiah 41:10

text: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.
author: Psalm 23:1

text: Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.
author: Matthew 5:4

text: And we know that in all things God works for the good of those who love him.
author: Romans 8:28

text: Do not let your hearts be troubled. Trust in God; trust also in me.
author: John 14:1

text: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself.
author: Matthew 6:34

text: Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you.
author: 1 Peter 5:7

text: When anxiety was great within me, your consolation brought me joy.
author: Psalm 94:19

text: Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous!
author: Joshua 1:9

text: The Lord your God is with you, the Mighty Warrior who saves.
author: Zephaniah 3:17

text: This is the day the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it.
author: Psalm 118:24

text: Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding.
author: Proverbs 3:5

text: Be still and know that I am God.
author: Psalm 46:10

text: Your word is a lamp for my feet, a light on my path.
author: Psalm 119:105

text: I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit.
author: John 15:5

text: Whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
author: Matthew 25:40

text: Let us not love with words or speech but with actions and in truth.
author: 1 John 3:18

text: Each of you should use whatever gift you have to serve others, as faithful stewards of God’s grace.
author: 1 Peter 4:10

text: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with you.
author: Luke 1:28

text: Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.
author: Luke 1:42

text: This is my body, which is given for you.
author: Luke 22:19

text: I am the bread of life.
author: John 6:35

text: Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.
author: Matthew 5:7

text: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
author: Revelation 21:4

text: Even though I walk through the darkest valley, I will fear no evil, for you are with me.
author: Psalm 23:4

text: Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.
author: Matthew 11:28

text: And the prayer offered in faith will make the sick person well.
author: James 5:15

text: We must go through many hardships to enter the kingdom of God.
author: Acts 14:22

text: Honor your father and mother.
author: Exodus 20:12

text: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast.
author: 1 Corinthians 13:4

text: As for me and my household, we will serve the Lord.
author: Joshua 24:15

text: In their hearts humans plan their course, but the Lord establishes their steps.
author: Proverbs 16:9

text: If any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously to all.
author: James 1:5

text: Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
author: James 4:7

text: No temptation has overtaken you except what is common to mankind.
author: 1 Corinthians 10:13

text: Always be prepared to give an answer to everyone who asks you to give the reason for the hope that you have.
author: 1 Peter 3:15

text: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
author: Matthew 28:19

text: For I am convinced that neither death nor life, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
author: Romans 8:38-39

text: And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.
author: Matthew 28:20

text: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the human heart.
author: Ecclesiastes 3:11

text: The Lord is my light and my salvation—whom shall I fear? The Lord is the stronghold of my life—of whom shall I be afraid?
author: Psalm 27:1

text: Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or terrified because of them, for the Lord your God goes with you; he will never leave you nor forsake you.
author: Deuteronomy 31:6

text: Though an army encamp against me, my heart does not fear; Though war be waged against me, even then do I trust.
author: Psalm 27:3

text: Whoever wishes to be my follower must deny his very self, take up his cross each day, and follow in my steps.
author: Luke 9:23

text: Pain and suffering have come into your life, but remember pain, sorrow, suffering are but the kiss of Jesus — a sign that you have come so close to Him that He can kiss you.
author: St. Mother Teresa of Calcutta

text: Without the burden of afflictions it is impossible to reach the height of grace. The gift of grace increases as the struggle increases.
author: St. Rose of Lima

text: A humble soul does not trust itself, but places all its confidence in God.
author: St. Faustina

text: Faith is to believe what you do not see. The reward of faith is to see what you believe.
author: St. Augustine of Hippo

text: I distrust a charity that costs nothing and does not hurt.
author: Pope Francis

text: Know that the greatest service that man can offer to God is to help convert souls.
author: St. Rose of Lima

text: The secret of happiness is to live moment by moment and to thank God for all that He, in His goodness, sends to us day after day.
author: St. Gianna Molla

text: Anxiety is the greatest evil that can befall a soul except sin. God commands you to pray, but He forbids you to worry.
author: St. Francis de Sales

text: Let no one mourn that he has fallen again and again: for forgiveness has risen from the grave!
author: St. John Chrysostom

text: The world offers you comfort, but you were not made for comfort. You were made for greatness.
author: Pope Benedict XVI

text: The Eucharist is the secret of my day. It gives strength and meaning to all my activities of service to the Church and to the world.
author: Pope Saint John Paul II

text: Nothing great is ever achieved without enduring much.
author: St. Catherine of Siena

text: In my deepest wound I saw your glory and it dazzled me.
author: St. Augustine of Hippo

text: I have found the paradox, that if you love until it hurts, there can be no more hurt, only more love.
author: St. Mother Teresa of Calcutta

text: We cannot all do great things, but we can do small things with great love.
author: St. Mother Teresa of Calcutta

text: The saints did not all begin well, but they ended well.
author: St. John Vianney

text: Hold your eyes on God and leave the doing to Him. That is all the doing you have to worry about.
author: St. Jane Frances de Chantal

text: The devil fears hearts on fire with love of God.
author: St. Catherine of Siena

text: To be tempted is a sign that the soul is very pleasing to the Lord.
author: St. Padre Pio of Pietrelcina

text: It isn’t good to let our thoughts disturb us or worry us at all.
author: St. Teresa of Ávila

text: Never be afraid of loving the Blessed Virgin too much. You can never love her more than Jesus did.
author: St. Maximilian Kolbe

text: If God sends you many sufferings it is a sign that He has great plans for you, and certainly wants to make you a saint.
author: St. Ignatius of Loyola

text: Our hearts were made for You, O Lord, and they are restless until they rest in You.
author: St. Augustine of Hippo

text: He who possesses God lacks nothing: God alone suffices.
author: St. Teresa of Ávila

text: Spread love everywhere you go. Let no one ever come to you without leaving happier.
author: St. Mother Teresa of Calcutta

text: Life with Christ is a wonderful adventure.
author: St. John Paul II

text: Be who God meant you to be and you will set the world on fire!
author: St. Catherine of Siena

text: True charity consists in doing good to those who do us evil, and in thus winning them over.
author: St. Alphonsus Liguori

text: Faith is like a bright ray of sunlight. It enables us to see God in all things as well as all things in God.
author: St. Francis de Sales

text: If you can’t feed a hundred people, then feed just one.
author: St. Mother Teresa of Calcutta

text: Fasting cleanses the soul, raises the mind, subjects one’s flesh to the spirit, renders the heart contrite and humble.
author: St. Augustine of Hippo

text: Fasting is the soul of prayer, mercy is the lifeblood of fasting. So if you pray, fast; if you fast, show mercy.
author: St. Peter Chrysologus
